homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name. 'GNAD' and 'nvdatabase.swarthmore.edu' are the census's other names for the entity (ML-03). The encyclopedia's title for the name redirects to George Lakey (B7 F42): the redirect makes a person's article the encyclopedia's entry for the name, and the person, whom the field names as the database's developer (F45), stays a distinct entity, never a sense of the name. The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the entity.
distinct_entities: George Lakey (person), activist, sociologist and writer, who developed the database with students (B7 F45, F46) and whose definition the review quotes (B4 F30, 'Lakey 2011c'); the Wikipedia title 'Global Nonviolent Action Database' redirects to his article (B7 F42)
Swarthmore College and its Peace and Conflict Studies Program, the Peace Collection and the Lang Center for Civic and Social Responsibility, its operator (B1 F2)
the Strategy and Nonviolent Struggle course, the research seminar whose students add cases (B6 F38, F40)
the Center for Nonviolent Conflict Research (CNCR, ICNC), whose resource library describes it (B3)
Discuss Data (Research Centre for East European Studies at the University of Bremen and Göttingen State and University Library), whose review of 8 May 2025 by Nathalie Rathkamp is card 4 (B4 F36)

the movements whose campaigns its waves group (the U.S. Civil Rights Movement, the student anti-sweatshop and living-wage movements and others, B2 F13, F14), which the database's unit rule keeps apart from its cases (B3 F17)

captures.description: THE DATABASE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The Global Nonviolent Action Database is a free online project hosted by Swarthmore College that catalogues more than 1,200 nonviolent campaign case studies from over 100 countries.' Scope and timeline; clusters; waves; search; origin (2011). Six cards: the database (two), CNCR, Discuss Data, Policy Commons, Swarthmore.
